questions.q: In this lab, why does `getOverdueDays(gr)` belong on the base class `TaskUtils` rather than directly inside `IncidentUtils`?
options: Because ServiceNow requires all GlideDateTime methods to live in a base class
Because IncidentUtils cannot have more than one method
Because due_date is a field every Task-derived record has, so the logic is genuinely general and reusable by Problem, Change, or Incident alike
Because base classes run faster than child classes
questions.explain: getOverdueDays only touches fields the Task table provides to all its children, so it's correctly placed in the general TaskUtils class.

questions.explain: Skipping the parent's initialize call means the parent's own setup never runs, breaking any inherited logic that depends on it.

questions.q: Why does the Incident table make a good real-world case for a base/child class design in this lab?
options: Because Task is a client-side-only table
Because ServiceNow requires every Script Include to match a table name exactly
Because Incident and Task are unrelated tables with no shared fields
Because Incident genuinely extends the Task table on the platform, inheriting fields like due_date — mirroring the TaskUtils/IncidentUtils relationship
questions.explain: Incident, Problem, and Change are all real specializations of Task on the platform — the Script Include hierarchy mirrors a real table relationship, not an invented one.

questions.q: In the Business Rule at the end of the lab, what does calling `new IncidentUtils()` once give access to?
options: Only getOverdueDays; isMajorIncident requires a second constructor call
Neither method, until the Script Include is manually activated
Only isMajorIncident; getOverdueDays must be called on a separate TaskUtils instance
Both the inherited getOverdueDays method from TaskUtils and the incident-specific isMajorIncident method, on the same object
questions.explain: Inheritance means one IncidentUtils instance already has everything TaskUtils provided, plus its own additions — that's the real payoff of extending a class.

questions.q: Per this lab's closing design check, what would a future ProblemUtils class get "for free" simply by extending TaskUtils?
options: Automatic major-incident detection, inherited from IncidentUtils
A new field added to the Problem table
Nothing — every class must reimplement getOverdueDays independently
The getOverdueDays logic, already written once, with no need to duplicate it inside ProblemUtils
questions.explain: Because getOverdueDays lives on the shared base class, any future class extending TaskUtils inherits it without rewriting it.
